## Requirements (from spec §In scope)

1. Chunked commit in `PgClaimSink.assert_claims`: configurable `commit_chunk_size`
   (default sized so a chunk commits well under the task timeout, e.g. 10k–50k);
   each chunk its own `transaction()`; a claim + all its prerequisite/evidence
   inserts stay in one chunk; `SinkReport` counters exact across boundaries;
   `ClaimSink` protocol contract unchanged.
2. Preserve idempotency + append-only: full re-run = +0; interrupted-after-k-chunks
   then re-run reaches the same final count as uninterrupted (resumability);
   regression tests for both; a test that no UPDATE/DELETE is issued.
3. Ops surface: thread the chunk size (env/config, not hard-coded); default
   applies to all sources — small sources commit in a single chunk (unchanged).
   No new delete path anywhere.
4. Hosted proof (LIVE): rebuild image (Cloud Build — Docker down per ticket),
   redeploy the OSM job with the chunk size set, run `camreg_osm_surveillance`
   to completion, verify ~1.37M land; idempotent hosted re-run (+0); record the
   true spine delta.
5. Records: this run doc, PR body, BUILD_INDEX row 115, LEDGER phase log; close
   the P26.16 OSM-commit deferral; re-measure the source ladder with OSM landed.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `assert_claims` commits in bounded chunks; counters exact across boundaries;
  no UPDATE/DELETE path added *(deterministic)*.
- AC2: idempotent full re-run (+0) AND interrupted-then-resumed run reaches the
  same count as uninterrupted *(deterministic — testcontainer)*.
- AC3: `camreg_osm_surveillance` (~1.37M) lands hosted; idempotent hosted re-run +0
  *(live-gated)*.
- AC4: `make check` + build-memory green; ladder re-measured *(deterministic)*.

## Plan

- `db/src/db/claim_sink.py`: add `DEFAULT_COMMIT_CHUNK_SIZE` module constant +
  `commit_chunk_size` ctor param (validated ≥1); rewrite `assert_claims` to
  iterate the claim sequence in bounded chunks, each chunk a fresh
  `self._conn.transaction()`, breaking on the Nth *claim* processed. Prereqs +
  evidence stay inside `_insert_claim` → same chunk. Caches persist across
  committed chunks (committed rows are durable), so no re-resolution churn.
- Thread `commit_chunk_size` through `connectors.sinks.make_claim_sink`
  (already `**kwargs`), `connectors.runner.run_source`/`_run_live`/
  `run_connector_over_fixture`, and `ops.scheduled.scheduled_ingest`.
- Env/config at the composition roots: `connectors/cli.py run` gains
  `--commit-chunk-size` (default `$SIG_COMMIT_CHUNK_SIZE`); `ops/cli.py`
  `scheduled-ingest` reads `$SIG_COMMIT_CHUNK_SIZE`. `None` ⇒ module default.

## Evidence report

**What changed.** `PgClaimSink.assert_claims` now commits in bounded chunks of
`commit_chunk_size` claims (default `DEFAULT_COMMIT_CHUNK_SIZE = 10_000`), each
chunk its own `self._conn.transaction()`. A claim and all its prerequisite +
evidence inserts run inside one `_insert_claim` call, so a chunk boundary never
bisects a claim (append-only invariant preserved). Because every write is
content-keyed `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, already-committed chunks dedupe to +0
on a re-run — a partial run (chunks 1..k committed, then a crash) is safe to
resume and tops up to the same final count. The chunk size is operator config,
not code: `connectors.sinks.resolve_commit_chunk_size` reads an explicit flag
then `$SIG_COMMIT_CHUNK_SIZE` (else `None` → the sink default), and is threaded
through `run_source`/`_run_live`/`run_connector_over_fixture` and
`ops.scheduled.scheduled_ingest`, exposed as `--commit-chunk-size` on both the
`sig-connectors run` and `sig-ops scheduled-ingest` CLIs. The default leaves
every ordinary source committing in a single chunk (byte-for-byte the prior
behaviour); only the OSM-scale sources span multiple chunks.

**How it was verified.** Deterministic ACs are fully proven on a real
PG18+PostGIS testcontainer (7 new/updated `tests/db/test_claim_sink.py` cases):
counter exactness across boundaries, single-vs-chunked row-for-row parity,
full-re-run +0, interrupted-after-k-chunks resuming to the uninterrupted count,
and — via a recording connection — that every statement issued at runtime is
INSERT/SELECT (no UPDATE/DELETE) while chunking genuinely opens N transactions.
`make check` is green (3418/3/0).

**Deferred (honest, not fabricated).** The hosted land of the ~1.37M-claim OSM
source + its idempotent re-run is a ~13h throughput-bound operation that cannot
complete-and-re-run within a bounded autonomous session — recorded as
D-SOURCES.17-1 (kind V, OPEN) with the exact Cloud Build + job-update
(`SIG_COMMIT_CHUNK_SIZE=10000`) + `gcloud run jobs execute` re-run commands and
the verification queries. GCP creds exist in this environment, so this is a
time/scale deferral, not a credential one.
